bad.title: Add to cart → reads as a link
bad.text: Plain text with an arrow says it opens the mug’s page. Some people expect to see it, not add it.

bad.title: A filled button for the same action
bad.text: Desk lamp gets a button and Mug gets a link. People wonder if they do different things.

good.title: The mug gets the same button
good.text: Same fill, same label, no arrow. People know what it does before they press it.

good.title: Built once, used in both places
good.text: A change to the button reaches the product page and the wishlist together.

bad.title: First it’s bookings
bad.text: Add to my bookings is the first name people learn for the saved hotel.

bad.title: Then it’s reservations
bad.text: A second word makes people wonder if a reservation is something else.
bad.wait: Press Add to my bookings to see this.

bad.title: And it lives under Trips
bad.text: There’s no Bookings tab, so people have to guess where the hotel went.

good.title: Add to Trips names the place
good.text: The button tells people where the hotel will go.

good.title: Added to Trips, the same word
good.text: The message confirms it in the words people just read.
good.wait: Press Add to Trips to see this.

good.title: The tab people look for
good.text: It matches the button word for word, and shows a 1 once the hotel is added.

bad.title: Delete sits where Cancel usually is
bad.text: People who press by habit erase the 3 photos they meant to keep.

bad.title: Cancel moved to the right end
bad.text: The spot most apps use for the main action now backs out.

good.title: Cancel on the left, as usual
good.text: A press by habit here keeps the photos.

good.title: Delete at the right end, in red
good.text: The main action sits where people expect it, and the red asks them to read first.

bad.title: Subscribe keeps its own 6px corner
bad.text: Rounder corners and Green both pass it by, so it keeps its corner and its blue.

bad.title: Free holds its own blue
bad.text: Switch the accent and the badge clashes with the card’s green top edge.

bad.title: Four parts didn’t follow
bad.text: Only the card changed. Badge, input, button and link each need their own edit.
bad.wait: Turn on Rounder corners to see this.

good.title: Subscribe follows the card
good.text: Its corner and fill come from the same tokens, so it changes with them.

good.title: Free turns green too
good.text: One accent change reaches the badge, the button, the link and the card’s top edge.

bad.title: A token named after its color
bad.text: The name blue-500 says what it looks like, not what it’s for.

bad.title: The rain turns green with the brand
bad.text: Every bar used blue-500 too, so the chart no longer looks like water.

bad.title: A blue token that holds green
bad.text: The name now lies, and fixing the rain means editing the chart as well.
bad.wait: Press Make the brand green to see this.

good.title: Named by job: accent and rain
good.text: Both point at blue-500 today, but each can change on its own.

good.title: The rain stays blue
good.text: The brand turns green, and the chart keeps the color people read as water.

good.title: One line changes
good.text: Only accent moves to green-600. Nothing else in the code is touched.
good.wait: Press Make the brand green to see this.

bad.title: Eleven tokens, 1px apart
bad.text: On a card, radius-7, radius-8 and radius-9 look alike, so people pick at random.

bad.title: Popular tokens with near twins
bad.text: Next to radius-8 and its 41 uses sit look-alikes with 3 and 2. That’s drift already.

good.title: Three steps people can tell apart
good.text: 4, 8 and 16px. The difference shows at a glance.

good.title: Each one says what it’s for
good.text: Cards is written right under radius-medium, so a new card needs no guess.

bad.title: Pay is one color among five
bad.text: Orange, blue, purple, red and green. People read every label to find Pay.

bad.title: Apply coupon shouts in orange
bad.text: It grabs the eye first, though most people have no coupon.

bad.title: Popular in warning red
bad.text: Red usually means a problem, so the insurance line looks like an error.

good.title: Pay is the only filled button
good.text: Full width at the bottom, so people find it without reading the rest.

good.title: Apply coupon goes quiet
good.text: Outlined like Back to cart. Still easy to find for people with a code.

good.title: Popular as a plain label
good.text: The tags stay readable but gray, so they don’t compete with Pay.

bad.title: Red, with no reason given
bad.text: Delete account and Upgrade share nothing, so nobody can tell when red fits next.

bad.title: Save changes turns red
bad.text: A teammate read red as important. Clear chat history, which deletes data, stays plain.
bad.wait: Press Build the next screen to see this.

good.title: A rule with a why
good.text: The reason lets the next person apply it to buttons the guide never listed.

good.title: Red lands on Clear chat history
good.text: The one action that deletes messages. Save changes stays the normal primary.
good.wait: Press Build the next screen to see this.

bad.title: Checkout’s corners came by copy
bad.text: Nobody chose 4px. It came along with an old screen.

bad.title: Settings copies a copy
bad.text: It takes Profile’s off blue and trims the padding. Each release adds a variant.
bad.wait: Press Next release to see this.

bad.title: The count climbs, nothing stops it
bad.text: Two releases later there are 6 button styles, and still only two were chosen.

good.title: An audit, part of the routine
good.text: Run audit checks every button against the standard one.

good.title: Drift folded back
good.text: Checkout’s 4px corners go back to the standard button.
good.wait: Press Run audit to see this.

good.title: Sign in with Apple, named
good.text: The one real variant becomes button-apple, so it stays on purpose.
good.wait: Press Run audit to see this.
